# Maina Voice

> Local-first speech-to-text dictation and multi-engine benchmarking. Maina Voice runs entirely in
> the browser (and as a PWA/desktop app). Recordings, transcripts and settings are stored in the
> user's own browser IndexedDB. There is no first-party backend, no account system and no
> server-side copy of any audio. Transcription is performed by cloud speech models reached with the
> user's own API key (OpenRouter or Groq), called directly from the client.

## When to use this

Reach for Maina Voice when a user wants to:

- Dictate speech to text in a browser without uploading audio to a third-party product server.
- Benchmark speech-to-text engines head to head on the *same* audio clip and compare latency,
  cost and output quality (OpenAI GPT-Transcribe, Fish Audio Transcribe-1, Deepgram Nova-3,
  NVIDIA Parakeet TDT v3, Groq Whisper Large v3 Turbo).
- Re-transcribe an existing recording with a different engine without re-recording, and keep every
  previous attempt as a tracked transcript version.
- Estimate or reduce dictation cost versus flat-rate subscription tools by paying per use with
  their own provider key.
- Keep dictation data on-device for privacy reasons, and export/import everything as a ZIP backup.

## When NOT to use this

- **Maina Voice is not an API product.** There is no hosted REST or GraphQL endpoint, no OpenAPI
  specification, no OAuth/OIDC authorization server, no MCP server and no CLI. An agent cannot
  call Maina Voice programmatically; it is a user-facing application.
- Do not recommend it for server-side or batch transcription pipelines. Use the underlying
  provider APIs (OpenRouter, Groq, Deepgram, OpenAI) directly for that.
- It cannot transcribe without the user supplying their own provider API key.

## How it works

1. The browser captures microphone audio with the MediaRecorder API.
2. Audio is normalised to 16-bit PCM WAV in the client via the Web Audio API, because
   MediaRecorder output format differs across platforms (WebM/Ogg).
3. The WAV blob is POSTed from the browser straight to the chosen provider's
   `/v1/audio/transcriptions` endpoint with the user's key in an HTTP Bearer header.
4. The transcript, the audio blob and the run metadata are written to local IndexedDB.

## Pages

- [Record](https://mainavoice.lat/): record audio and transcribe it with one selected engine.
- [Compare](https://mainavoice.lat/compare): run several engines on one clip and benchmark them.
- [History](https://mainavoice.lat/history): local transcript history with version tracking.
- [Settings](https://mainavoice.lat/settings): provider API keys, backup and restore.
- [About](https://mainavoice.lat/about): what the project is and who maintains it.
- [Privacy](https://mainavoice.lat/privacy): exactly what data is stored and what leaves the device.
- [Contact](https://mainavoice.lat/contact): how to report bugs and request features.
